section_summary: This section brings together a historical survey of international fisheries disputes and 1937 reports on Japanese fishing activity in East and Southeast Asia and the Pacific. The reports describe Japanese trawling around Hong Kong and the Philippines, a proposed expansion to Panama, and the aims and rules of a Japanese oceanic fisheries association. Several intervening pages are file notes directing readers to related records.

subfiles.title: Acting Secretary of State's transmittal to the Secretary of Commerce
subfiles.about: Transmits a Tokyo despatch on Japanese views concerning an international agreement for fishing in Bering Sea and Bristol Bay.
subfiles.summary: Encloses despatch No. 2108 and a translated Japanese press account.

subfiles.title: Note on paper about fishing rights as a source of international disputes
subfiles.about: Calls attention to a paper on fishing rights and indicates that a copy is being sent to Tokyo.
subfiles.summary: Describes Mr. Stheer's paper as informative and notes its circulation to Tokyo.

subfiles.title: Summary of Fisheries Disputes
subfiles.about: Surveys historical conflicts over fishing, whaling, territorial waters, and fur seals, and the agreements or arbitration used to settle them.
subfiles.summary: The survey traces fisheries disputes from early Scottish, English, Dutch, and Danish claims through North Atlantic fishing controversies and Russian and American assertions in the Bering Sea. It emphasizes recurring disagreement over the extent of coastal jurisdiction and describes treaties, conventions, and arbitration awards that addressed particular disputes. Its conclusion argues that international agreements and arbitration can resolve conflicts that threaten relations between states.

subfiles.title: File note on proposed investigation of Japanese fishing in Mexican waters
subfiles.about: Points to a memorandum on a proposed investigation of Japanese fishing in Mexican waters.
subfiles.summary: Notes that the investigation was discouraged because Mexico and Japan might distrust it.

subfiles.title: File note on Japanese salmon fishing in American and Canadian waters
subfiles.about: Points to a despatch enclosing a Japanese association's defense of salmon fishing in American and Canadian waters.
subfiles.summary: References despatch No. 2328 and a translated pamphlet reported in the Japan Advertiser.

subfiles.title: File note on Japanese trawlers supplying Calcutta
subfiles.about: Points to a report on Japanese trawlers supplying fish to Calcutta and other Asian ports.
subfiles.summary: Reports an experiment involving 40 trawlers, with other vessels serving Rangoon and Singapore.

subfiles.title: Division of Far Eastern Affairs summary of Hong Kong despatch No. 509
subfiles.about: Summarizes Japanese dominance of fishing around Hong Kong and activity in Philippine waters.
subfiles.summary: Highlights Japanese equipment, Hong Kong fishing ranges, Chinese competition, and licensed Japanese boats in the Philippines.

subfiles.title: Japanese Activities in the Fishing Industry of South China and the Philippines
subfiles.from: Howard Donovan, American Consul, Hong Kong
subfiles.about: Reports the scale and methods of Japanese trawling around Hong Kong and Chinese fishermen's response.
subfiles.summary: Donovan describes the Horai Fishing Company's fleet, equipment, bases, and voyages around South China and as far as Western Australia. He reports that Chinese fishermen and dealers formed a guild after losing trade to better equipped Japanese vessels, and sought a subsidy from authorities in Nanjing. He encloses a memorandum on Japanese fishing in the Philippines.

subfiles.title: Activities of Japanese National Fishermen in the Fishing Industry in the Philippines
subfiles.about: Details licensing, ownership, fishing grounds, and methods of Japanese fishermen in the Philippines.
subfiles.summary: Lists 1936 boat and fisherman licenses, suspected Japanese ownership, fishing grounds, and Manila, Iloilo, and Cebu markets.

subfiles.title: Japanese Attempts to Extend Fishing Activities to Panama
subfiles.from: Richard F. Boyce, American Consul, Yokohama
subfiles.about: Reports efforts to register Japanese fishing boats under the Panamanian flag for fishing off Panama.
subfiles.summary: Boyce reports a proposed voyage of the Amano from Japan to Panama and the Panamanian consul's reluctance to approve registration.

subfiles.title: File note on Japanese Association for the Development of Oceanic Fisheries
subfiles.about: Points to a despatch containing the association's articles and list of directors.
subfiles.summary: Identifies Tokujiro Koshida as association president and references despatch No. 2379.

subfiles.title: Articles of the Kaiyo Gyogyo Shinko Kyokai
subfiles.about: Sets out the objectives, membership rules, officers, and administration of an association promoting deep-sea fishing.
subfiles.summary: The articles establish an association to promote deep-sea fishing inside and outside Japanese territorial waters and to shape policy and public opinion. They specify membership classes and dues, grounds for losing membership, and procedures for choosing directors and council members. The text on page 587 ends while listing employees.
